headline: The row boundary condition makes the entire matrix one sorted row-major sequence
statement: Return whether target appears in matrix. Each row is nondecreasing and the first element of a row is greater than the final element of the preceding row. The matrix is rectangular. Use O(log(rows*columns)) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
constraints: Matrix values and target range from -10,000 to 10,000
intuition: The row boundary condition makes the entire matrix one sorted row-major sequence. Binary search it without allocating a flattened copy.
approach: Convert a midpoint i to row i//columns and column i%columns.
Compare its value with target and discard the impossible half.
correctness: The flattened sequence is sorted by both row order and the row boundary rule. Each binary-search comparison removes values all smaller or all larger than the target; if present, the target stays in the remaining interval until found.

complexity.explanation: Time O(log(rows*columns)); auxiliary space O(1). Output storage is excluded unless stated.

pitfalls: This stronger row boundary condition differs from Search a 2D Matrix II.
Divide by the number of columns, not rows.
Use mid-1 or mid+1 to make progress.
